evals.name: cross-boundary-contract-drift-on-vm-change
replacement-crawl-must-assert-its-floor
evals.prompt: Picking up ACME-930: 'Automated crawl of every page in the back-office menu — replaces the manual back-office click-through checklist (18 pages)'. My plan: global setup signs in as the test user and saves the menu endpoint's response; the spec file generates one Playwright test per menu leaf; each test asserts HTTP 200, no console errors, no failed API calls, and that `main` contains some visible text. If the menu comes back empty, setup throws. The back-office section only appears in the menu when the user has the admin role. Grill the slice before I write it.

evals.name: story-with-criteria-but-no-approach
evals.prompt: Picking up ACME-412: 'Warehouse staff can put an order on hold, with a reason, so it isn't picked.' Acceptance criteria: (1) Given an order that hasn't been picked, when staff put it on hold with a reason, it disappears from the pick list and the order page shows 'On hold' with the reason. (2) Putting an order that's already picked on hold is refused, with a message saying why. (3) Releasing a held order puts it back on the pick list. Architecture is settled: ADR-0014 says order states live on the Order aggregate in Acme.Warehouse.Domain, and commands are MediatR handlers under Acme.Warehouse.Application/Features/Orders. Nobody has written an approach yet. Grill the implementation.
assertions: Drafts an approach before the grill slate and marks it as a draft
The approach says how each of the three acceptance criteria is met
Runs the lenses on its own draft: raises at least one real question or fix about it (e.g. hold racing a pick in progress, the refusal's error contract, cancellation)
Drafts automatic test cases per criterion covering positive, negative and edge cases, each labelled with the criterion it traces to
The pick-list test asserts that the specific held order is absent, not merely that the list changed or is non-empty
Does not re-open the settled architecture (where order state lives, the handler style)

evals.name: story-handoff-parked-questions
evals.prompt: Picking up ACME-501, created by grill-architecture from the pause-subscription feature. Story: 'Customer pauses their subscription from the account page'. Acceptance criteria: (1) a paused subscription is not charged at its next renewal; (2) the account page shows 'Paused until <date>'; (3) pausing an already-paused subscription is refused with a message saying until when it's paused. Dependencies: needs ACME-503 (Billing recognises the Paused status) to ship first. Settled architecture: ADR-0021 puts the pause state on the Subscription aggregate in Acme.Subscriptions.Domain, set by a PauseSubscription MediatR command under Acme.Subscriptions.Application/Features/Subscriptions. Parked for grill-implementation: (c) how the account page gets the pause end date without a second request — it loads through the existing GetAccountOverview query; (d) how Billing's renewal job skips paused subscriptions without one status request per subscription. Approach on the story: add PausedUntil to the aggregate and a Pause(until) method that refuses when already paused; PauseSubscription handler loads, calls Pause, saves. Grill the implementation.
assertions: Puts parked question (c) on the slate and answers it against the existing GetAccountOverview query (e.g. extend its projection with the end date)

Recognises that parked question (d) is about Billing's renewal job, which ACME-503 builds: moves it to that ticket instead of settling the job's query or testing it here. Pinning down the contract this slice exposes to ACME-503 is fine
Treats the ACME-503 dependency as a sequencing constraint or blocker, without re-opening where the pause state lives
Does not re-open ADR-0021 (aggregate placement, command style)
Maps each of the three acceptance criteria to test cases labelled with the criterion they trace to
